body: Seems related to https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/1310, but the last comment there indicates that that issue was fixed back in 2016.
I have tried on colab with TF version 1.14 and was able to reproduce the issue.Thanks!

The following code works:

```
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

do_error = True

with tf.Graph().as_default() as graph:
    my_var = tf.Variable(np.ones(5), use_resource=True)
    # Moved tf.gather outside the tf.device block.
    gather = tf.gather(my_var, [0, 2, 4])
    with tf.device("/gpu:0" if do_error else None):
        gather = tf.identity(gather)
    opt_op = tf.train.MomentumOptimizer(0.1, 0.1).minimize(gather)

with tf.Session(graph=graph) as sess:
    sess.run(tf.global_variables_initializer())
    sess.run(opt_op)
```

The only change here is that the `ResourceGather` op is no longer placed on GPU. This makes sense since we want to place all ops touching a resource on the same device. If this is the desired behavior we could change `sparse_read` to place the `ResourceGather` op on the same device as the handle.
However, I tried removing the optimizer in the original code, and it started to work. So I am not sure whether my understanding is correct. @alextp or @mrry may have more ideas.

I think this is “working as intended”, but the error message is a little overwhelming. The root of the problem is that `ResourceSparseApplyMomentum` only has a CPU implementation, and it must run on the same device as where the variable is stored. For efficiency, `tf.gather(my_var, …)` uses a `ResourceGather` op that also must run on the same device as where the variable is stored. However, if you explicitly request that `tf.gather(my_var, …)` be placed on GPU, we are left with an unsatisfiable set of constraints.

Saurabh’s workaround [above](https://github.com/saxenasaurabh) is correct, but it has the unfortunate effect of copying the entirety of `my_var` from CPU to GPU on each step, which is likely to impair performance.

As a short-term workaround, you can enable “soft placement”, which should fall back to placing the ops on the CPU when no GPU implementation is available, by passing `config=tf.ConfigProto(allow_soft_placement=True)` to `tf.Session`.

Longer term, it would be useful to add GPU implementations of `ResourceSparseApply*`, wherever possible. I think we’d welcome contributions for those.

Thanks for the explanation @mrry. Do you think it makes sense to change [`sparse_read`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/ec64a3e0c7d86a52ee166e4998a376e1112fc3c6/tensorflow/python/ops/resource_variable_ops.py#L638) to place the `ResourceGather` on the same device as the resource handle just like we do for [`read_value`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/ec64a3e0c7d86a52ee166e4998a376e1112fc3c6/tensorflow/python/ops/resource_variable_ops.py#L632) and ignore the device context? That way this won't error out.

> Do you think it makes sense to change sparse_read to place the ResourceGather on the same device as the resource handle just like we do for read_value and ignore the device context? 

That probably makes sense! Historically we’d have used `with ops.colocate_with(my_var):` for that. Technically the `with ops.device(self._handle.device):` [in `read_value()`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/ec64a3e0c7d86a52ee166e4998a376e1112fc3c6/tensorflow/python/ops/resource_variable_ops.py#L632) isn’t sufficient because if `self._handle.device` isn’t a complete device specification, then you wouldn’t be guaranteed to colocate them.

True. I believe [placer](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/4db2480e44dc82de7ff22bb5ffbb562d24fa9930/tensorflow/core/common_runtime/colocation_graph.cc#L614) might colocate them though so maybe the undefined specification is better than an incorrect one. I'll send out a fix.

The placer should already force-colocate the sparseread and the resource
handle, both in eager and graph modes.
